item_description:
Ornamental lotus drawing in the center of the cover page.
Below the drawing the note: spyod 'jug yig xxxx sna bzhugs lags so written in dbu can. "sna" possibly stands for "sna tshogs bzhugs lags so," indicating a text belonging to various categories.
Script: 'bru tsha.
Lines per folio: 8; 7 on the last folio.
Folio numbers above 10 written with the decimal in letters and the units as a number (except "five," which is written in letters).
Orthography:
- frequent broken shad
- frequent abbreviations
- bindu for -m
- Tibetan numerals written in cyphers
- superabundant 'a suffixes (e.g., dbye' ba)
Some corrections in dbu can (e.g., fol. 2a6). Numerous interlinear annotations in dbu med and dbu can, that appear to be more frequent at the beginning of the text. Below 4b7, some numerals apparently counting the sa bcad divisions. Long annotation at the bottom of fol. 12b, with a reference sign repeated on 12b7.
Several annotations identifying scholars that are not named in the text are preceded by the same sign.
Frequent ornaments between gnyis shad and bzhi shad. sbrul shad used on fol. 2a1, and rgya gram shad in the middle of 3a6, 13b5, 17a3 and 23b6. Ornament containing a pebble and a sbrul shad in the middle of fol. 15b5.
On the color images (bdr:MW14345) one can see some expressions written in red ink (with vowels in black) and some expressions highlighted in yellow.
